subject: Crosswalk: Dedicated capacity demo slot & throughput/QoS negotiation
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@aerofy.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Demo request — Dedicated capacity for search-indexing workload

Hi Jonas,

I signed up through the trial earlier today and indicated we'd like to see a demo focused on Dedicated capacity. We're evaluating options for pushing search-indexing inference into production and want to understand Redwood's throughput and latency profile for sustained workloads.

Quick context: Aerofy is a mid-market SaaS (search + analytics). Our plan is to feed batches of ~50 tokens per request, average 1.5k qps sustained for indexing during business hours with spikes to ~4k qps. Latency target: 95th <= 300ms if possible. Also curious about multiregion/failover behavior.

Can you run a focused walkthrough and a short validation test? We're in PST (San Francisco) and would prefer a morning slot next week (Apr 5–9).

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
CTO, Aerofy
alex.morgan@aerofy.com

--
(Attachment stub: capacity-snapshot.png)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@aerofy.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-01T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — Dedicated capacity for search-indexing workload

Alex — thanks for the context and welcome aboard. I read your qps/latency targets and we can absolutely structure a dedicated demo that focuses on throughput, steady-state concurrency, and failover behavior.

Two quick asks before we lock a slot:
- Can you confirm average tokens per call and typical batch sizes (you mentioned ~50 tokens — is that consistent?),
- Do you expect per-request KV-cache reuse across sessions or mostly independent short-lived requests?

Proposed windows (all PST mornings):
- Tue Apr 6, 9:00–9:45am PST
- Wed Apr 7, 9:30–10:15am PST
- Thu Apr 8, 8:30–9:15am PST

Ben (cc) will run the calendar handoff and prep the MAP doc. We can include a short single-region validation run and a quick dual-region behavior sketch if you need failover profiling.

If any of those times conflict, let us know a couple alternatives and Ben will coordinate.

—Jonas
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@aerofy.com>

Thanks, Ben and Jonas. Apologies — I misstated the timezone in my first note. We're actually UTC-4 this week (we have an east coast office). Early morning PDT works but we need the slot to be 11am–noon our time (which I think is 08:00–09:00 PDT).

Confirming additional details you asked for:
- Tokens per request: 45–55, median ~50.
- Typical pattern: primarily independent short-lived requests (indexing calls from workers), with a small percentage (~5%) that reuse the same session/context for KV-cache advantages.
- Expected steady-state: 1.5k qps; peak bursts up to 4k qps sustained for 30–120s.
- Latency requirement: 95th <= 250–300ms for index-append path.
- Compliance: we'll need a high-level SOC2 and data-segmentation walkthrough. Attached is our security checklist (aerofy-security-reqs.xlsx).

We prefer Redwood to run the validation workload using a synthetic corpus that approximates our token distribution — easier for us on short notice. Recording is fine.

If Tue 9:00 PDT is no longer the right mapping, can you confirm a slot that maps to Aerofy 11:00–12:00 EDT next week?

Thanks — Alex

(Attachment: aerofy-security-reqs.xlsx)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com

Alex — perfect, that clarifies things. We can do the slot that maps to Aerofy 11:00–12:00 EDT. Proposed confirmed time: Wed Apr 7, 11:00–11:45 EDT (08:00–08:45 PDT).

Plan for the session:
1) 10m intro + high-level architecture and SOC2/data segmentation overview (Jonas)
2) 20–25m focused dedicated-capacity demonstration: steady-state throughput, spike test, and 95th latency sampling (Ben + Ops)
3) 10–15m mutual action plan and next steps including quant metrics we'll capture.

Pre-call deliverables:
- Redwood will run a synthetic workload matching: median tokens 50, steady 1.5k qps, 30–120s bursts to 4k qps.
- We'll attach a one-page MAP with roles, success criteria, and a staging run checklist (MAP-dedicated-demo.docx).
- I've uploaded a short capacity snapshot and will include Zoom + HubSpot links below.

Fallback: if dual-region validation isn't possible in the initial run, we'll run a single-region stress test and schedule a quick follow-up to exercise failover.
